blocks.text: Quick verdict

Decodo is the better choice for scraping, SERP tracking and e-commerce monitoring: a large published pool, deep targeting, near-perfect benchmark success rates, a free trial and clear prices ($35 for 10 GB, $275 for 100 GB). Proxys.io is the better choice for fixed identities in multi-account, affiliate and social media work, for cheap bulk IPv6, and for flat-rate mobile proxies with unlimited bandwidth, backed by a 24-hour refund window. The two complement each other more than they compete.

Proxys.io and Decodo both sell residential, mobile and datacenter proxies, but their core models are different. Proxys.io rents individual IPs, from $0.13 for IPv6 to a few dollars for premium residential IPv4, usually with unlimited bandwidth. Decodo sells access to a 115M+ rotating residential pool by the gigabyte, with city, ZIP and ASN targeting and scraping APIs. This comparison helps you decide whether your work needs fixed identities or rotation at scale.

blocks.text: Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

PROXYS.IO offers both rented static addresses and a rotating residential network. The provider reports more than 100 million ISP addresses across 195 countries, country/region/city targeting, up to 100 saved parameter sets and rotation every 2-60 minutes. Its mobile service covers 14 countries with city/carrier selection and roughly 2,000-5,000 addresses per country/carrier combination. Static IPv4 covers 24 markets. These are supplied specifications, not independently measured availability. HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 are included on every plan.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
Decodo in 2026: what you get

Decodo (formerly Smartproxy) sits between the budget brands and the enterprise giants. It gives every customer the full 115M+ residential pool, city and ZIP targeting, and a self-service dashboard that most people can configure in minutes. Proxyway's annual tests ranked its pool second only to Oxylabs in size among the providers it tested, at a price well below enterprise level, which is why Decodo shows up on almost every shortlist.

Strengths: Large 115M+ pool at a mid-market price; Near-perfect success rates in independent tests; Clean, fast self-service onboarding; Scraping APIs available when raw proxies are not enough. Weak spots: Plan traffic does not roll over; Published pricing stops at 100 GB; beyond that you need a quote; More expensive per GB than budget brands.
Pricing: Proxys.io vs Decodo

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

Decodo sells residential traffic at $4/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, or on monthly plans: 3 GB for $11.25 ($3.75/GB), 10 GB for $35, 25 GB at $3.25/GB, 50 GB for $150 and 100 GB for $275 ($2.75/GB). Top-ups are billed at your plan's rate, so you are not pushed into the next tier.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; Decodo comes to about $35. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; Decodo comes to about $275. Both Proxys.io and Decodo work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

PROXYS.IO reports a residential pool of 100M+ ISP addresses; this has not been independently audited. Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses and Decodo lists '115M+'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage countries and Decodo lists 195+. On targeting, Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile, while Decodo offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile, and Decodo offers rotating or sticky sessions with configurable duration. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?
General web scraping: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: a large pool and near-perfect benchmark success rates. How Proxys.io compares: it is a per-IP shop, not a large rotating pool.
SERP and rank tracking: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: a dedicated SERP scraping API plus city targeting. How Proxys.io compares: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks.

Social media and multi-account management: Proxys.io. Proxys.io has the edge here. Why: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. How Decodo compares: sticky sessions, sub-users and an easy dashboard.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: ZIP targeting and a ready-made e-commerce API. The limitation on the Proxys.io side: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: wide coverage with city and ASN targeting. How Proxys.io compares: limited geo depth.
Tight budgets: Proxys.io. Proxys.io has the edge here. Why: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth. How Decodo compares: it is mid-priced, not cheap.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. Decodo: Free trial (about 100 MB) on residential. Verification and payment rules differ too. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. Decodo: Light KYC; checks on some targets. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Proxys.io and Decodo before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Proxys.io and Decodo is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial; Decodo: free trial (about 100 MB) on residential).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Proxys.io comes out ahead in 2, Decodo in 4, and 0 are ties. That makes Decodo the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs, while Decodo is strongest for small and mid-size scraping teams. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
